steps.title: Meet the Arduino Uno
steps.markdownContent:
Pick up your **Arduino Uno** board and hold it gently by its edges, just like holding a tasty cracker! 🍪

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **The #1 Golden Hardware Rule: ALWAYS UNPLUG BEFORE REWIRING!**
> Whenever you insert, remove, or adjust jumper wires and electronic components, disconnect the USB cable first! Moving wires on a powered circuit can cause accidental metal-to-metal shorts that blow out the microcontroller or trip your computer's USB port.

> [!TIP]
> **ESD (Static Electricity) Protection:** Touch an unpainted metal object (like a table leg or computer case) before picking up circuit boards to safely discharge any static electricity built up on your clothes or carpet.

Look closely at the board. Notice these important landmarks:
1. **USB Port**: The shiny silver metal box. This is where you plug in the cable to send code and power from your computer!
2. **Power Jack**: The round black socket. You can plug in a battery pack here when your robot is on the move.
3. **Reset Button**: The small push button in the corner. Pressing it restarts your program from the very beginning.
4. **Built-in LED**: A tiny light labeled **'L'** right on the board next to Pin 13.
5. **Pin Headers**: The long rows of black plastic sockets with little holes along the edges.

steps.title: Board Architecture & Key Landmarks
steps.markdownContent:
### Exploring the Arduino Uno Hardware Map 🗺️

Take a close look at your board. Every component has an important job:

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ [USB Port]                [Digital Pins 0 - 13]        │
│  Silver Box               Header along the top edge    │
│                                                        │
│ [Reset Btn]   [ATmega328P Chip]           ['L' LED]    │
│  Tiny button   Big black rectangle         On Pin 13   │
│                                                        │
│ [DC Jack]     [Power Header]    [Analog Pins A0 - A5]  │
│  Round socket  5V, 3.3V, GND     Smooth sensor inputs  │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

#### Why Are These Landmarks Special?
- **USB Port (Silver Box)**: Delivers 5V electricity and sends compiled code into the board's flash memory.
- **DC Barrel Jack (Black Socket)**: Allows untethered battery power (7V–12V) so your robot can zoom around without a computer cable.
- **ATmega328P Microcontroller**: The big rectangular black chip with metal legs. This is the master processor holding your program!
- **Pin Headers**: The socket rows where jumper wires connect your external buttons, buzzers, and LEDs.

steps.title: Drag & Match Board Landmarks
steps.markdownContent:
### Put Your Board Knowledge to the Test! 🎯

Inspect your physical Arduino Uno board, then match each label badge to its corresponding landmark below:
- **USB Connection**: Silver port that links to PC for flashing code & 5V power.
- **DC Power Barrel Jack**: Black round port for external 9V battery or wall adapter.
- **Digital Pins (0–13)**: Top header pins sending & receiving binary HIGH/LOW.
- **Analog Pins (A0–A5)**: Bottom right pins reading smooth variable voltages.

Drag each badge into its slot to complete the hardware inspection!
